pr_records.title: WIP: RF Geolocation — no-token native TV pairing, USB hardware discovery and natural map navigation
pr_records.body:
### 2026-11-06 — TV pairing and map drag / RTL-SDR control transfers

- Removed legacy manual token-entry UI for native Hauppauge DVB-T/T2/C and read-only FM RDS/DAB bridge. **Connect TV tuner → local approval window** uses the already implemented explicit allowlisted localhost pairing; the bridge still requires opt-in startup and refuses unauthorized origins. GitHub Pages cannot directly operate a Linux DVB kernel frontend via WebUSB.
- Added **Identify TV USB** on the main Hardware panel. Browser permission/discovery only; native `/dev/dvb` adapter listing and actual scan remain separately verified.
- Map drag previews with pointer capture and GPU-translated tile/marker overlay; prevent text selection and prefetch one border tile to reduce blanks while panning.
- Actual RTL2832U RF capture and FM sweeps now report the exact hardware step (gain, tuning, sample buffer or I/Q read) at which the `setRegBuffer` / control-transfer error occurs, release their own broken session when appropriate, do not retry automatically and never invent measured RF levels or location.
- Updated offline PWA cache to v22 and added regression tests for pairing, USB detection, natural pan and hardware transfer error status.
- Scoped `gh-pages` synchronization verified, preserving the other applications' subtrees. CI/hardware acceptance are independent checks: native USB/RF and DVB physical tests are not claimed complete.


### Nov 6, 2026 — natural drag, no-copy TV pairing and RTL-SDR recovery

- Main **Find My Location / Hardware** panel now has **Connect TV tuner** + **Scan TV**. Actual Linux /dev/dvb frontend + sysfs USB vendor/product identity is discovered through the user-owned loopback companion; the static Pages website does NOT claim or decode Hauppauge DVB hardware as WebUSB.
- The native helper is started by the user with `python3 -m rf_geolocation_center.native serve --enable-pages-bridge`. The TV Connect button opens a **localhost approval popup**; the user clicks **Approve this tab**. A cryptographic nonce and exact-origin postMessage deliver the temporary API credential without typing/copying tokens, persisting credentials or putting them in URLs. Old manual input remains collapsed under Advanced for fallback.
- Native bridge retains origin allowlist, explicit opt-in for official Pages, token authorization for each API call, DNS rebinding Host checks and private-network CORS preflight. No scan runs without a separate click; no arbitrary shell execution, open LAN port or automatic Linux driver takeover.
- Earth Map now pans with immediate visual layer translation on pointer move, commits exact geographic coordinates once on release and zooms around mouse pointer for wheel/double-click gestures.
- **Recover SDR** explicitly releases only this page's RTL2832U WebUSB handle then attempts exactly one reconnect to an already-permitted device, to recover from errors such as `setRegBuffer failed block=0x1 reg=120`. This does not guarantee hardware-level recovery, stop readsb, alter Linux modules or fake RF samples.
- Tests added for local approval security/CORS, main TV controls, natural map gestures and one-shot RF error recovery. PWA shell v21; browser/hardware field acceptance remains open.

## Map tower provenance, clicks and real FM reference energy probes (2026-11-06)

- **Fixed the actual T-pin interaction bug**: the SVG marker overlay had pointer events disabled, so tower hover/click/keyboard selection was inaccessible. Updated marker-only hit testing and prevented map-pan pointer capture from swallowing marker clicks. On hover, show catalog-vs-RF summary; on click, show exact coordinates, whether from OpenStreetMap vs antenna measurements, published FM/TV frequency tags, any real I/Q/decoded RDS/DVB overlap and its limits, plus the original OSM record.
- **Map-to-RF workflow**: known-frequency FM tower candidates have a "Measure / calibrate RF source" action that selects/adds the candidate in the existing real RTL-SDR survey and opens independent known-distance calibration. Missing site frequency or actual hardware observation cannot produce a ring.
- **RF-only unknown-area status**: visible NO FIX until data sufficient for a separate experimental calibrated RSSI model. Catalog points, DVB channel lists, ADS-B transmitted aircraft coordinates, orbit predictions and raw power peaks are NOT observer locations.
- **FM energy control channels**: real user-triggered RTL-SDR spot tests for published NRW FM channels including WDR 2 Köln 98.6 MHz, 1LIVE Köln 87.6 MHz, WDR 2 Langenberg 99.2 MHz, WDR 2 Bonn 100.4 MHz and WDR 3 Langenberg 95.1 MHz, sourced from WDR frequency information. The app never claims that energy proves RDS identity or known distance.
- **FM sweep fix**: the bounded sweep now covers all 206 100 kHz channel centers across 87.5–108 MHz rather than stepping 200 kHz and missing 98.6 MHz; single-channel probes merge into the prior scan log and frequency matches use a 15 kHz center tolerance.
- **Map responsiveness**: cache projection center, viewport and RF match table once per render instead of repeating DOM layout reads for every range-circle point or tower. Added interaction, hardware and frequency regression tests. Updated offline service-worker cache **v19**. Pages subtree synced without overwriting other applications.

### TV and other RF capabilities
- Existing feature branch native **Hauppauge WinTV-soloHD** TV scanning uses an explicitly started localhost Python/DVBv5 bridge, access token and native Linux DVB frontend. There is no direct DVB tuner scan from static Pages alone. Real DVB services are mapped to OSM sites only as frequency-overlap *candidates*, not established transmitter IDs or user-location evidence.
- The same page exposes Text Center already-decoded FM RDS/DAB metadata and direct Flight Radar local ADS-B aircraft, keeping them separate from stale internet positions. It doesn't start a second RTL-SDR while another application owns the device.

### Current release gate
- Changes remain on draft PR #16, not merged to main. Syntax/HTML sanity checks passed; GitHub RF CI and physical SDR/Hauppauge/browser acceptance must be verified before claiming full device functionality.

### Map geometry / USB hardware picker fix (November 6, 2026)

- **Fixed warped T markers and range rings**: the Earth Map SVG viewBox now follows the rendered element's exact pixel dimensions (previously constant 900x520 with independently stretched axes), preserves circles in any browser aspect ratio, redraws via ResizeObserver and declutters overlapping catalog towers. OSM tiles remain separate.
- **Main-screen Hardware · Add and connect your receivers** panel: actual Chromium WebUSB `requestDevice({filters:[]})` picker, previously permitted USB devices via `getDevices()`, visible USB VID:PID and product information, direct connect from a permitted Nooelec RTL2832U row, receiver-specific WebUSB permission/claim self test, release and dedicated GNSS Web Serial controls. No DevTools paste.
- Selecting a USB device grants browser permission only; it does NOT claim the dongle, take over a Linux DVB driver, decode signals or provide a position. The generic picker may omit protected TV USB interfaces. Hauppauge TV devices remain native Linux DVB/metadata import only; no fake direct WebUSB DVB scanning.
- Radio / TV Scan has a separate direct RTL receiver chooser using the same underlying hardware controller, never a second concurrent SDR claim. USB cleanup and Hard Stop stay local to this app.
- Updated localhost allowlist and offline service worker **v17**, with new source files and regression coverage. Browser screenshot and physical hardware acceptance remain to be verified on user machine.

## Simplified UI — updated November 6, 2026

**Preview:** https://tihulu.github.io/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/rf_geolocation_center/

The old multi-panel science dashboard was too complicated. Geolocation Center now opens **Find My Location**, with one large real Earth Map and two compact multi-select panels:
- **Position methods**: GPS/Device (browser/OS or dedicated NMEA receiver), Nooelec RTL-SDR (experimental RF-only), Hauppauge WinTV-soloHD 01589 (DVB-T/T2/C).
- **RF reference layers**: Ground transmitters, aircraft and satellites. Each checkbox controls actual corresponding map layers. Real device fix, RF-only model estimate, historical cached coordinates, mapped catalog candidate, real local ADS-B and internet aircraft are clearly distinguished.
- Actions: **Find My Location**, **Scan selected receivers**, **Show measured rings**. No fictional rings in the default view. RF-only excludes OS/GPS, mixed selection supports independent overlays. User preferences persist locally.
- **Radio / TV Scan** is a second simple screen. There is a visible existing WebUSB authorized Connect RTL-SDR control (not a fake hardware connection), an on-demand OSM broadcast site lookup and real 87.5–108 MHz RF energy sweep, Hard Stop, compact top candidate sites and real scan frequency results, Back to map.
- Sites with explicitly tagged FM frequencies are automatically added as UNVERIFIED candidate references; catalog lookup and antenna RF power are not direct distance measurements. Manual entry, calibration and TDOA remain in collapsed **Advanced** panels; all original science sections remain accessible from **Advanced Tools** in the sidebar.

### User's Hauppauge TV receiver
- Amazon ASIN **B0152XLPFS** identified as **WinTV-soloHD model 01589**. Official Hauppauge specifications support DVB-T/T2/C, not GNSS, ADS-B or DVB-S satellite.
- Nearby **OpenStreetMap television broadcast towers** are now discovered alongside FM towers. DVB service frequencies imported from Hauppauge native scans are matched only against explicitly published TV MHz tags as **UNVERIFIED possible transmitter sites**; incomplete OSM metadata or TV channel numbers never generate fabricated frequencies, distances or user positions.
- Native Linux DVB receiver file import implemented: **Radio / TV Scan → Import real DVB scan metadata** reads user-produced DVBv5 .conf channel lists and shows real channel name, frequency, delivery standard, service/network IDs. Actual file import never implies known transmitter coordinates or a verified self-position.
- Optional script **scripts/dvb_scan_linux.sh** runs the genuine Linux **dvbv5-scan** utility against a compatible /dev/dvb frontend using a real regional initial tuning file. The helper doesn't disable the Hauppauge DVB kernel driver or invoke GPS. Direct TV scanning from GitHub Pages requires a user-authorized local native backend, not yet implemented. False browser hardware access is never claimed.

### Existing GPS/RF modes preserved
- Browser location with permission; dedicated GNSS NMEA serial/file; independent orbital catalog prediction; RTL-SDR WebUSB sampling; experiment-only calibrated RSSI range hypothesis rings; real ADS-B aircraft via same-origin Flight Radar BroadcastChannel; separate internet OpenSky references; OSM tower candidates; independent field provenance and offline cache.
- Cached position is never a new fix, GPS vs Wi-Fi source is not disclosed by browser geolocation.
- No automatic accurate RF/TV standalone positioning is claimed: unique emitter identification, calibrated timing/direction/ranges or true GNSS-SDR tracking still require implementation and physical validation.

### Tests and integration
- New DVBv5 parser and simple map UI regression tests; browser module syntax, DOM element references and balanced HTML verified.
- PWA shell cache **v21** includes simple UI, TV parser and Linux scan helper.
- Feature branch PR remains **draft**, separate from main. GitHub Pages scoped /rf_geolocation_center/ directory synchronized without changing other app subtrees.
- CI and real hardware + browser field validation remain release gates.

pr_records.title: Unified Radio/TV Channel Center: real full scans, selectable DAB audio, editable channel lists and simpler UI

## Continuation of PR #14 → PR #13, preserving all current features
The previous single Radio Data page mixed RF diagnostics, FM, DAB, TV, ASR and media controls. This draft separates a straightforward Scan → Channel Library → Play / Record / Edit workflow from advanced RF tools.

### Radio Center P410
- Search & filter FM and DAB decoder-confirmed stations, mark favorite, rename label, hide, and choose sort order; preferences persist separately from immutable verified station metadata.
- Play real FM from channel list via existing rtl_fm/ffmpeg, optional recording.
- DAB+ decoder services now have **in-app PLAY** through safe same-origin /api/dab/audio/{sid} proxy to fixed 127.0.0.1:7979 /mp3/{sid}, after verifying live welle-cli FIC audio service; no fabricated playback. DAB current-mux Refresh also adds verified stations to library.
- Expand managed DAB tune block presets from four to all 5A–13F.
- FM "Full" 87.5–108 MHz survey with up to 128 actual RDS trial candidates; cannot guarantee non-RDS stations are identified.
- DAB full 5A–13F FIC discovery and persistent station directory retained; no scan automatically begins.

### TV Center P420
- Real Linux DVB-T/T2 regional table **full scan** using installed dvbv5-scan, user-selected frontend, separate actual hardware, explicit consent, duration bounds and browser heartbeat timeout.
- Store only real DVBv5 service data after successful scanner exit.
- DVB-discovered TV channels are **not yet playable** until separately authorized local MPEG-TS relay supplies the stream; configured relay channels remain playable/recordable.
- TV channel list uses same search / favorites / aliases / ordering.

### UI & safety
- Side navigation Radio Center, TV Center, Advanced RF; overview CTAs. Move technical diagnostics under accessible details; stop duplicating live players.
- Preserve AI, translator, captions, MOT, RDS, flight radar, satellite, browser WebUSB and Global HARD STOP.
- No silent driver/OS process stop, no cross-app lease broker claim, no destructive DB updates or RF metadata rewriting. No automatic RF operation on app launch.
- GitHub Pages direct WebUSB still cannot execute local DAB/TV decoder or driver operations.
- Documented limitations and physical acceptance: docs/END_TO_END_CHANNEL_UI_AUDIT_2026-11-06.md.
- Tests: decoder parse, channel preference persistence, safe stream URL, full FM candidate cap, API gating, platform smoke; hardware acceptance remains pending.

pr_records.title: Consolidate FM/DAB receiver lifecycle and add zero-install GitHub Pages WebUSB radio
pr_records.body:
## Purpose
Continue, not restart, Text Center. Start on current main 45abc5c (preserve WebUSB-first Satellite Center README), integrate draft PR #8/#10/#11/#12 without wiping AI, translator, live FM/TV and desktop work.

## Integrated
- FM and DAB verified-station auto scan, continuous FM audio/no-ASR fallback, genuine MOT gallery and archive, safe local installer
- PR #11 app-owned DAB start/stop, managed cleanup, receiver status and `STOP ALL TEXT CENTER RF`, plus newly integrated FM/DAB scanner stop paths
- PR #12 unified media controls, Flight Radar antenna/internet/hybrid source attribution, offline language packs, desktop entry points and static Pages
- Pages Direct USB: WebUSB RTL2832U permission, experimental mono FM via AudioWorklet, volume, optional local MediaRecorder download, bounded .cu8 I/Q
- Satellite Center browser-only receiver page mirrored into `docs/satellite/`, original Satellite Center PR #9 remains untouched
- Static PWA assets and regression check; original AI compute, speech, translation and postprocessing preserved

## Browser-only limitations (explicit)
GitHub Pages does not run Python, ffmpeg, readsb, welle-cli, or OS services. Direct WebUSB is supported on selected desktop Chromium browsers under HTTPS and only if drivers/USB permissions permit. Firefox/Safari cannot use WebUSB. Experimental FM audio has not been verified on physical hardware. DAB/MOT/RDS, ADS-B decoding, DVB television and local AI need additional supported decoder/model runtimes, or a trusted user-managed companion. Raw I/Q != protocol decode. External readsb/welle-cli processes are never automatically stopped.

## Publishing gate
GitHub Pages repository settings require owner to choose Deploy from branch `integration/consolidated-pages-webusb-2026-11-06` folder `/docs`. Site URL is expected at https://tihulu.github.io/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/ but not yet verified live.

## Validation
Run Python 3.11–3.13, JS syntax, installer safety, synthetic HTTP/ownership and cross-platform smoke in GitHub Actions. Physical Nooelec FM/DAB/MOT/recording/cleanup, Hauppauge DVB, macOS/Windows USB, Raspberry Pi and offline AI acceptance gates still pending. **Do not merge to main** before physical gates. Full matrix: `docs/CONSOLIDATED_PAGES_WEBUSB_ACCEPTANCE_2026-11-06.md`.

Cross-repo references preserved: Flight Radar PR #7; Survival Kit PR #10; planning PR #6.

pr_records.title: Add managed DAB Start/Stop and Stop All Own RF with close/heartbeat cleanup
pr_records.body:
## Request
The user wants every antenna-using Tihulu application to release its receiver when closed and to expose internal service Start/Stop controls. An observed `readsb` process was holding the Nooelec dongle and blocking Text Center FM/DAB. This must never be solved by indiscriminately killing external processes.

## Implemented
- `textcenter/managed_dab.py`: starts only an explicitly authorized **app-owned welle-cli** child (selected Band III channel), refuses busy USB / occupied port 7979 / missing decoder, and stops only that process group. Browser-specific owner token + short server watchdog lease: when the owning tab closes or heartbeat expires, its DAB worker is released. An **external welle-cli/readsb** remains untouched.
- New Radio Data **START FM RADIO**, **STOP ALL TEXT CENTER RF**, **START DAB RECEIVER** and **STOP DAB RECEIVER** controls, along with current managed service status. Existing dedicated FM/RDS/TV/manual spectrum start/stop remains.
- CSRF-gated `/api/dab/manage/start|stop`, `/api/receiver/stop-all`, read-only ownership and heartbeat status. Browser pagehide attempts an owned-only close; the server watchdog handles tab crashes. Server close and normal SIGTERM also release managed DAB.
- STOP ALL stops this server's own FM/RDS/survey/audio/live radio/TV and managed DAB only; never touches independent readsb, tar1090 or independently launched welle-cli.
- Mock-only tests for ownership, external conflicts, STOP, URL validation and same-origin API controls.

## Important limits / integration gate
- The existing generic pagehide paths for manual FM/RDS/TV are retained; a complete multi-tab owner/refcount lease broker is still required for Survival Kit. App-owned DAB **is** tab-owner scoped. A browser crash may delay release up to the 18-second watchdog TTL; no client-only hook can guarantee immediate release.
- Physical SDR USB release after closing welle-cli has not been verified on the user's Pop!_OS desktop. GitHub CI is synthetic.
- This branch is based on main; **PR #8 auto-scan and PR #10 FM/MOT/audio/installer** plus parallel translation/AI changes must be integrated additively without overwriting them. Keep Draft until those conflicts and physical tests are resolved.
- Do not merge anything to main or force-push other branches.

pr_records.title: Keep FM audio alive without ASR, add actual DAB MOT slideshow and safe one-line installer
pr_records.body:
## User-reported regression
On Pop!_OS / Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5, **Live FM Radio & Subtitles** showed the GPU/CPU detected but no installed speech runtime and no audible playback. The user checked *Enable live transcription* + *Translate speech live*. In `LiveFM.start`, an unavailable `SpeechPipeline` raised `SpeechError` during startup and aborted the **whole FM audio receiver**, even though ASR must be optional. They also require genuine **DAB MOT slideshow**, one-line install/update, and non-conflicting integration with another agent simultaneously developing translation/compute/ASR.

## This isolated feature branch
- **Fix continuous FM audio independence:** optional missing Whisper/ASR runtime/AI model no longer terminates `rtl_fm → ffmpeg → browser` and MP3 recordings; status reports `subtitles_active=false` with `subtitle_unavailable_reason`. Never fabricate captions or auto-download AI models.
- **FM browser diagnostics:** add SHOW AUDIO PLAYER action, connection status, and actionable media load/decoding errors. The existing persistent media dock and opt-in recording stay.
- **Actual DAB MOT (not Internet artwork):** read already-running loopback welle-cli, archive timestamped/source-attributed genuine JPEG/PNG slides, distinguish not broadcast vs saved vs decoder error, support standard Band III blocks, add optional manually started locally cached slideshow to Radio Data (400) and Live Radio (410). No background RF polling or receiver retuning, and reject new DAB sync while Text Center is actively using the same RTL-SDR for FM.
- **One-line installer + update:** `install.sh` creates user-local launch and updater wrappers, checks optional external dependencies, does not use sudo, activate RF, start a background daemon, or download models. `--update` requires clean checkout and fast-forward only; preserves SQLite/media and recordings. See README for one-line feature-branch test command.
- **AI work isolation:** no changes to `textcenter/compute.py`, `speech.py`, `transcripts.py`, `postprocess.py`, `live_tv.py`. Separate instructions: [integration handoff](docs/INTEGRATION_HANDOFF_FM_DAB_MOT_INSTALL_2026-11-06.md).

## Verification
Mock tests cover missing versus available speech runtime and real-format MOT image state; shell installer is syntax/static checked, plus existing Python/JS checks. **Real audio playback and MOT capture on the physical SDR have NOT been validated yet.** User must stop welle-cli when testing FM, and stop FM before new DAB MOT sync. A saved DAB slideshow can display while FM plays offline, but live FM and a different-frequency DAB MOT cannot be received simultaneously with one dongle.

## Merge gate
Draft/unmerged. Wait for the parallel translator agent to finish; then rebase/merge **additive hunks only** onto the latest main, preserving all new translation, FM/TV, NPU/GPU and recording changes. Run complete Python 3.11–3.13 CI, JS syntax, shell syntax, and physical Firefox FM audio/MOT tests before publication. Do not merge/reset/force-push or change the other agent's branch.

pr_records.title: Satellite Center: GitHub Pages + cross-platform localhost SDR companion and one-line installs
pr_records.body:
## TIHULU Satellite Center — standalone companion + GitHub Pages bridge (v0.2 draft)

This is a continuation of the existing standalone Satellite Center. No changes to the Survival Kit, Flight Radar or existing Text Center routes. The PR remains DRAFT for hardware acceptance.

### Added
- **Same repository GitHub Pages** static browser UI, with a sibling URL for both `main/(root)` (`/satellite_center/`) and `main/docs` (`/satellite/`). No replacement Pages deploy workflow.
- **Cross-platform Python 3.11+ localhost receiver service** on 127.0.0.1:8791: Linux Debian/Ubuntu/Pop!_OS, Raspberry Pi OS ARM32/ARM64, macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64.
- Browser-hosted UI controls real local SDR through **user-paired 256-bit bearer token**; exact allowed origin, loopback Host, CORS preflight, CSRF. Password never embedded in URLs or static Pages and is never pushed to GitHub.
- macOS/Windows portable process start/stop and file locking; Linux keeps the shared Text Center SDR lock.
- Explicit one-line user-local installers `satellite_center/install/install.sh` and `install.ps1`, shortcuts to browser-backed local program. No silent USB driver changes, RF scan or background daemon.
- Paired browser download of modest-size archive files without revealing tokens in URLs. Large IQ captures downloaded locally.
- Existing ISS, Meteor, amateur/CubeSat and Iridium tracking, time-bound RF capture, pass scheduling, APRS and SatDump integration unchanged.

### Pages availability
Pages link is **not advertised as already live**. This draft branch must be merged/published and the repository's existing Pages publishing source checked in Settings → Pages. Full instructions: `satellite_center/WEB_AND_INSTALL.md`.

### Security / privacy
- Pages cannot directly control USB without the local companion.
- Device acquisition remains receive-only with explicit action/scheduled user approval; no private Iridium traffic decoding.
- Local CSRF, HTTP Host/origin allowlists, user-paired token, loopback-only listener.
- Phones reach their own localhost, not the desktop's localhost. Mobile remote access requires a separate authenticated HTTPS gateway.
- Safari may block HTTPS Pages → local HTTP; use local UI.
- Scheduler executes **only while companion process runs**; user login-autostart services are not installed without opt-in.

### Testing
- 7 synthetic local unit tests PASS (original 5 + CORS/pairing 2).
- Python compileall, shell bash -n, browser JS node --check PASS on local source.
- Actual SDR hardware, Windows native driver, macOS ARM and Raspberry Pi hardware acceptance **not yet performed**. Separate RTL-SDR CLI and drivers required; SatDump/multimon-ng optional.

### One-line install (draft branch)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/feature/satellite-center-standalone-2026-11-06/satellite_center/install/install.sh | bash
```
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/feature/satellite-center-standalone-2026-11-06/satellite_center/install/install.ps1 | iex
```
Review remote scripts before running and use a normal user account.

### v0.2.2 — Safe SDR release on application/tab close
- All Satellite Center-owned RF subprocesses (including APRS decoder chains and SSTV rtl_fm) tracked and terminated on explicit Stop/Quit, Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and normal server close; cooperative receiver lock released at capture exit.
- Hosted/local UI **Quit companion & release SDR** button shuts down service; browser pagehide immediately asks to stop **manual** capture. Abandoned manual browser captures time out after ~14 seconds without client heartbeat.
- Deliberately scheduled passes **continue when only a browser tab closes** and local companion remains running; full companion quit stops active scheduled reception and leaves future jobs saved for restart.
- Absolutely no kill/stop operations on third-party Flight Radar/readsb/welle.io/Gqrx processes. If readsb owns the USB SDR, closing Satellite Center cannot free it; readsb must be stopped separately.
- Synthetic tests: 13 PASS locally, including two owned subprocesses, owner vs unrelated client stop, failed browser departure watchdog, and authenticated Quit API. **Hardware testing still pending.**
- Hosted UI change has also been published to the existing `gh-pages` branch, but GitHub Pages settings still need to be enabled by repository owner if not already active.


### v0.2.3 — First-run USB wiring and pairing UX
- Pages and localhost dashboard now provide 5-step **Connect your USB SDR** guide: insert Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5 USB, attach correctly matched SMA antenna, install/run local companion, reveal the 64-character pairing token from localhost and connect hosted UI.
- OS-specific install commands and radio-tool hints for Pop!_OS/Debian/Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS, Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon; clipboard copy and actionable invalid-token error.
- Opt-in `POST /api/usb-test` runs bounded `rtl_test -t` only after local receiver lock and readsb conflict checks; stops its own child, reports USB-open evidence **not RF/satellite detection**, and needs genuine rtl-sdr tools/driver. Synthetic safety tests added.
- Amazon ASIN **B0152XLPFS** confirmed as **Hauppauge WinTV-soloHD 01589**, a DVB-T/T2/C terrestrial/cable TV receiver. Documented in compatibility section **as TV hardware only**, never treated as an RTL-SDR or Iridium/Meteor receiver. Existing Text Center DVB hardware module already recognizes Hauppauge candidates.
- Static updated HTML copied to the existing `gh-pages` `/satellite_center/` and `/satellite/` paths; main and unmerged standalone architecture untouched.
- Inline JavaScript syntax parsed successfully. Cross-platform GitHub Actions jobs currently queued; no physical USB acceptance claimed.


### Browser-only WebUSB mode (v0.3 experimental, no local software required)
- A **new static direct-USB frontend** is in `satellite_center/browser/` and is also published on `gh-pages`.
- Primary public URL `/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/satellite_center/` now redirects to browser-only `/satellite_center/browser/`; original Pages bridge stays at `/satellite_center/companion/`. No merge of the Python companion into main.
- The HTML page requires **only a supported Chromium browser + WebUSB permission + OS-accessible local RTL2832U/R820T receiver**; no Python, localhost server, setup token or package installer. It dynamically imports version-pinned `@jtarrio/webrtlsdr@3.0.7` via an HTTPS module CDN.
- Real device-open, setSampleRate/centerFrequency, resetBuffer and `readSamples()` operations; bounded original CU8 download (128 MiB), time-limited manual capture, relative uncalibrated power plot, USB stop/release on tab-hide/pagehide.
- Uses browser-only `satellite.js@6.0.1` and explicit CelesTrak TLE fetch (2h cache gate per tab) or local TLE file upload to compute geometric elevation/pass windows; session-only **foreground browser-open** scheduled scan.
- **Not implemented browser-only:** decoded Meteor images, APRS/SSTV text/images, dependable unattended pass execution after browser closure. Browser auto OS-driver fixes are impossible. Firefox/Safari do not implement WebUSB; Windows WinUSB driver and Linux DVB driver/udev setup may still be necessary. These limitations are disclosed directly in the UI; no fake RF reception.
- Direct WebUSB hardware test is still pending; JS syntax check is verified; a static acceptance contract and cross-platform CI JS syntax check have been added. External CDN availability was not verified in a physical browser.


### Satellite Center custom icon & Firefox/COSMIC dock support
- New user-requested radio-reception **V-dipole + RTL-SDR USB + satellite** artwork, with actual 192px and 512px optimized PNG plus scalable SVG. Asset paths: `satellite_center/browser/icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon.svg`, and `satellite_center/assets/tihulu-satellite.(png|svg)`.
- Static Browser-only Pages app now includes favicon, Apple touch icon and installable Chromium PWA manifest (standalone), along with an explicit OS **Applications / Dock** installation explanation and optional `beforeinstallprompt` UI.
- One-line Linux/Pop!_OS installer registers `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/{512x512,scalable}/apps/tihulu-satellite.*` and creates distinct menu shortcuts for **TIHULU Satellite Center** (Chromium WebUSB app window) and **TIHULU Satellite Center (Local Companion)**. Other programs/receivers are not stopped.
- Firefox support is accurately scoped: no native WebUSB and no Linux PWA install; orbital planner works in Firefox, **real USB reception requires the optional localhost companion**. Experimental WebUSB polyfills require extra native host installs and are not offered as zero-install.
- Pages `gh-pages` deployment and main README/guide updated independently of the draft PR. GitHub CI now checks icon asset dimensions and portable installer syntax. Real physical WebUSB/COSMIC dock behavior remains user hardware acceptance pending.


### v0.4 — Earth/sky satellite reception planning maps (6 Nov 2026)
- Added original **Heavens-Above-style polar azimuth/elevation sky view** (N up/E right, 0° horizon/90° zenith, selected ±15-minute sky trace) and **OpenStreetMap ground view** (TLE-derived subpoints, station marker, ±45-minute ground track, optional minimum-elevation contact footprint).
- Shared live/simulated TLE state with existing CelesTrak/locally imported ISS/Meteor/CubeSat/Iridium pass planner; includes ±45/+90-minute time slider, selected satellite details, source TLE age warnings, family and candidate SDR band filters, and receiver preset selection without starting a capture.
- **Data integrity:** geometry and compatible band are not RF reception. A measured I/Q session remains unattributed; CubeSat-specific downlinks must be checked against SatNOGS rather than guessed from a TLE. Iridium private traffic decoding remains excluded.
- **OSM rules/privacy:** Leaflet 1.9.4 lazy-loaded on deliberate map activation using SRI; standard OSM raster tiles from official endpoint, visible attribution, only viewport tiles, no cache bypass or offline/bulk fetch. Adjusted HTML referrer policy from no-referrer to strict-origin-when-cross-origin per OSM tile policy. Sky chart makes no OSM request.
- No local install or WebUSB permission is required for the geometry charts; Firefox can display maps even without WebUSB.
- Source: `satellite_center/browser/satellite_maps.mjs`, `satellite_center/MAPS.md`, `tests/test_satellite_maps.mjs`. Static JS parsing + 11 geometry/HTML checks passed during implementation. Node regression tests added to cross-platform CI.
- Published to existing `gh-pages` branch at `/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/satellite_center/browser/`; main app and Survival Kit unmerged and untouched. **Real browser map rendering/physical reception not hardware-validated yet**.


### v0.5 — Permissioned device location, offline DE/TR city typeahead, worldwide online lookup, fully custom stations (Nov 6, 2026)
- Replaced preset-only station entry with **custom coordinates by default**, explicit **Use device location (GPS / Wi-Fi)** (never auto-prompts), an accessible keyboard-navigable city search drop-down, optional country filter and **8,084 bundled DE/TR cities/towns** (7,104 German and 980 Turkish GeoNames-derived locations). Turkish/German accent folding, aliases and duplicate-name administrative distinctions are supported.
- User-selected **Search worldwide online** calls Open-Meteo's GeoNames-backed Geocoding API. **Online suggestions while typing are opt-in and off by default**, cancellable and debounced; no city text is sent to external APIs during normal offline autocomplete. GPS coordinates are never submitted to the online city search.
- Manually editable latitude/longitude remain fully supported (−90 to +90 / −180 to +180) anywhere worldwide. Explicit geolocation errors retain the prior observer without guessing. Actual browser location may originate from GPS/Wi-Fi/network and has estimated accuracy.
- Changing station invalidates old pass calculations and updates Earth/Sky reference coordinates; it never starts an SDR capture.
- Added ODbL 1.0 attribution for the derived dataset from `srestre/world-countries-cities-db`/dr5hn in `CITY_DATA_LICENSE.md`, and credit/licensing note for Open-Meteo (non-commercial free API).
- GitHub Pages was atomically updated with the new HTML/CSS/JS modules and bundled `cities-de-tr.json`; independent Python/SDR companion and main Text Center backend remain untouched.
- Offline matching spot-checks passed (Köln/Cologne, Hürth, İzmir and Karaburun). Browser-only GitHub checks PASS. Portable CI suite includes `tests/test_satellite_location.mjs` but latest runner jobs are queued; real client GPS permission dialog/OS environment is not yet physically validated.


### v0.6 — Blank OSM map recovery, sortable pass lists and minute-accurate scheduled RF analysis
- Diagnosed the blank Earth map screenshot: Leaflet satellite markers/track paths rendered, but OSM raster tiles did not. Added explicit OSM-compliant origin referrer, real tileload/tileerror status, retry controls, and automatic fallback after 3 tile errors or 9 s without a loaded raster tile. Bundled public-domain Natural Earth 1:110m land geometries (127 features) allow useful Earth context without relying on an external raster provider. Manual **Base map → World outlines** also handles blocked/403 images that may arrive as HTTP 200. No adblock bypass or tile prefetch.
- **Satellite pass calendar sorting**: next/soonest, latest/farthest date, elevation ascending/descending, duration ascending/descending, name and satellite-family filters. Removed 100-record pass truncation; paginates the full computed set 40 at a time.
- **Earth/Sky satellite sidebar sorting**: elevation, nearest/latest calculated next pass, range nearest/farthest and name, unknown next passes ordered last.
- Replaced the old one-click broken Schedule action with a user-confirmed **date/hour/minute** input (explicit browser timezone), frequency, duration, sample rate and raw IQ optional flag. The job is only in memory; no unattended/background claim.
- **WebUSB schedule executor**: releases an idle device after arming; at the due wall-clock minute (if page remains visible) tries to re-open only previously permission-granted 0bda:2838 RTL-SDR via `navigator.usb.getDevices`, then reads actual CU8 samples, creates uncalibrated digital-level min/mean/max/variation/byte count report and optionally attempts a local IQ download. Latest scheduled IQ can be downloaded manually again. Explicit preflight, countdown, optional screen wake lock, blocked/missed/stopped states and in-pass retry. Multiple jobs execute sequentially. No other process such as `readsb` is stopped.
- New ground station coordinates invalidate prior passes AND automatically cancel armed future jobs created for old ground station.
- **Limitations**: browser-only does not decode Meteor LRPT/APRS/SSTV or guarantee closed-tab/hidden/asleep work. Local companion remains optional for longer-lived schedules and external decoders. No physical Nooelec acceptance testing on user machine.
- Tests: JS module syntax, DOM ID parity, representative sort/schedule transitions, relative IQ analysis, 127-feature Natural Earth geometry all passed locally. Added Node CI regression tests for sort, scheduling and OSM fallback thresholds; relevant GitHub Actions portable matrix was still queued at last check. All new static assets published to `gh-pages`, source feature remains draft, main backend untouched.


### v0.7 — Resolve blank Earth map and make real RTL-SDR I/Q testing visible
- Fixed recurring blank-earth behavior by adding an always-visible browser-native **Canvas world map**, drawn from the existing 127-feature, public-domain Natural Earth GeoJSON shipped on GitHub Pages. Neither Leaflet nor OSM raster tiles are required for this primary geographic view. Earth tab immediately draws it, with station marker and clickable satellite ground subpoints; Leaflet/OSM is now a separate optional expandable interactive street map.
- Fixed previous Leaflet Natural Earth renderer to explicitly use an SVG renderer in a pane above raster tiles, and added **Test map background** diagnostics (local geometry count, canvas render, optional Leaflet SVG paths).
- Added visible **Test real USB + RF samples (3 sec)** button and a genuine WebUSB receiver probe: open previously permissioned RTL2832U, tune to the selected frequency, read actual I/Q sample blocks, report byte count/spread and uncalibrated relative digital level, then close the USB device even after failure. Does not stop readsb/Gqrx or claim named-satellite detection.
- Found and corrected a concrete receiver bug in every prior browser capture flow: `@jtarrio/webrtlsdr@3.0.7` returns `SampleBlock {frequency,directSampling,data:ArrayBuffer}` from `readSamples()`, rather than a bare ArrayBuffer. Manual and scheduled captures and the new probe now extract `.data` correctly. Upstream contract: https://github.com/jtarrio/webrtlsdr/blob/main/src/rtlsdr/rtldevice.ts
- Added `usb_live_probe.mjs` with short bounded real USB reads and synthetic mocked-driver tests in `tests/test_satellite_real_usb.mjs`, added to portable matrix CI. App / map / probe syntax, DOM IDs, sample block decoding, 127-feature geographic dataset and Pages/source parity were checked. Real device and real browser tests on the user's hardware still pending.
- Added query-version cache busting for the entrypoint, CSS and updated modules so installed app/Pages clients do not continue to run the older blank-map or broken-SampleBlock bundle. Published fixes on separate `gh-pages`; draft PR remains unmerged to main.


### v0.8 — WebUSB interface claim triage for Pop!_OS (Nov 6, 2026)
- Isolated reported `RadioError.UsbTransferError: Could not connect to the RTL-SDR stick...` to upstream `RtlCom.claimInterface()` calling `USBDevice.claimInterface(0)` (no tuner tune/readSamples reached). This is a separate problem from the earlier `SampleBlock.data` read bug.
- Added **Test USB interface claim (open → claim → release)** in the expandable USB diagnostics. It uses `navigator.usb.getDevices()` for a previously permitted 0bda:2838/2832 only, opens the device, selects config 1 if absent, claims interface 0, then releases/ closes its own handles in finally. Reports actual stage, native `DOMException.name`, underlying error message and cleanup warnings; no RF capture and no service/driver modification. Copy troubleshooting report includes the latest outcome.
- Existing driver failure now surfaces nested `error.cause` from upstream, not only generic RadioError. Added synthetic mock tests for successful claim cleanup, failed claim cleanup, unrelated device exclusion and nested errors.
- Actual resolution requires the user to check if `readsb`/another app or Linux DVB USB driver owns the RTL-SDR and release it via OS; GitHub Pages / WebUSB permissions cannot detach a kernel driver or stop services. Never automatically run `sudo`.
- Published new controls/module to existing `gh-pages` with cache-busted browser entrypoint. Real affected Pop!_OS USB interface has not been tested directly; no false claim of resolution.


### v0.11 — Fix blank OSM/Leaflet pane (screenshot showed tileload but opaque dark map)
- **Concrete UI root cause:** global `canvas { background:#091523; width:100%; margin:13px 0; border:... }` styled Leaflet's internally managed vector overlay canvas. That opaque canvas can cover already-loaded raster tiles and distort map geometry; the UI misleadingly reported successful tiles.
- Scoped chart styling to `#level-chart`, removed global canvas styling, and explicitly reset `#earth-map .leaflet-pane canvas` to transparent, marginless and without responsive sizing or decorative borders.
- Changed Leaflet `preferCanvas:true` to `preferCanvas:false` so satellite paths render as SVG; existing Natural Earth SVG world outlines remain an explicit separate renderer/pane.
- Expanded the optional `<details>` and waited two `requestAnimationFrame` ticks before initializing Leaflet, then called `invalidateSize`; added a `toggle` handler to update map sizing whenever the panel reopens.
- Corrected raster-status copy: a successful network `tileload` means a tile image was received, **not** proof of visible map content. `Test map background` now reports actual tile image dimensions, map size, SVG/marker counts and any opaque canvas overlays, without silently switching the user's basemap choice.
- Added `tests/test_satellite_leaflet_css.mjs` to cross-platform CI; local Chromium synthetic style check observed **before** opaque `rgb(9,21,35)` with 13px margins vs **after** transparent `rgba(0,0,0,0)` with 0px margins. This verifies the identified CSS regression, not a full network-backed Leaflet screenshot.
- Updated and published all map/HTML/CSS/entrypoint files to `gh-pages` with explicit `v=20261106-leaflet-css-v11` cache invalidation; no backend merge, no software installation. Actual user Brave/OSM integration still needs an on-device visual check.


### v0.12 — Display satellite markers, trajectories and coverage on the *interactive OSM map* (6 Nov 2026)
- Root cause of the reported map screenshot: OSM raster imagery and station marker were visible in an observer-centred regional viewport, but selected RADIO ROSTO/RS15 orbital subpoint (~59.6°N 42.9°E) and many of the 25 tracked objects were *outside* the camera bounds. Existing code also drew only a selected track; coverage was previously unchecked by default.
- Wired real **Focus selected satellite** / **Show all satellites** buttons, and automatic fit to current filtered TLE satellite positions on first map load (including when TLEs arrive later). Clicking a satellite in the list or map now pans/zooms the Earth view to its subpoint. **Center on ground station** still provides local regional view.
- **Orbit tracks:** all/selected/off, ±45-minute TLE propagation. **Coverage:** selected/all/off, geometric contact footprint based on current minimum elevation. Layer panes use explicit z-orders: Natural Earth 350, coverage 380, orbit tracks 420, clickable satellite markers 450, ground-station marker 470.
- The viewport status counts predicted markers currently on screen and reports the selected satellite when it lies outside bounds. At global overview, Leaflet can zoom to level 0–1; OSM zoom 0 is available, avoiding an artificially restricted Germany-only viewport.
- Standalone Node test `tests/test_satellite_earth_overlays.mjs` added to portable CI; static JS parse and representative geometry/DOM/overlay checks passed during implementation. GitHub Pages static assets synced with feature source under cache version `20261106-overlays-v12`.
- Geometric predictions are **not RF signal receptions**, and the update does not touch radio drivers, scan schedules, or the Text Center backend. Final visual acceptance in the user's Brave browser remains pending.

### v0.13 — OSM satellite overlays and local CU8 I/Q analysis
- Earth map fits the global TLE-derived satellite positions rather than remaining zoomed into Cologne with zero in-view ground subpoints. Show all / Focus selected camera controls added.
- Orbit tracks toggle All / Selected / Off (±45 min), coverage circles toggle Selected / All / Off, with separate Leaflet z-indexed satellite/track/coverage panes; native Natural Earth map draws the same paths. All are geometry only, not RF detections.
- New browser-only CU8 I/Q analysis section automatically analyzes the latest real raw WebUSB capture after download; previously downloaded CU8 files can be imported and analyzed locally without upload. Produces 2048-bin complex FFT, sampled waterfall, relative digital level over time, offset/frequency peak, DC/clipping statistics, and JSON report export.
- Bounded 32 × 4096 byte stratified sampling for potentially 128 MiB recordings. CU8 contains no frequency, rate or timestamp metadata; TIHULU filename is the only supported inference. No calibrated RF dBm, satellite identity or APRS/Meteor decoder claims.
- Added IQ analysis core/UI modules, synthetic FFT/file tests and cross-platform CI; browser scripts and HTML DOM controls syntax/parity verified. Synthetic +64 kHz tone yields measured +64 kHz peak.
- Published atomic updated assets to gh-pages with versioned module paths. Hardware/actual Brave chart rendering still needs user verification; main Text Center integration untouched.
### v0.14 — Live satellite tracking runs continuously after Now / live
- LIVE mode propagates cached TLE positions using the real wall clock at 1-second intervals while the browser tab is visible. Earth/OSM markers, local Canvas overview, polar sky positions, coverage outlines and selected details are updated; no RF receiver is opened.
- Geographic ±45-minute trajectory calculations are cached in 15-second slots; parsed TLE satellite records are reused across live frames and refreshed only when orbital lines change. Leaflet markers and polylines are updated in place to avoid full-layer redraw flicker.
- Added an explicit Pause button, a status indicator, a frozen timestamp simulation mode on time-slider interaction, and Now / live resume. Follow selected satellite while LIVE is opt-in and off by default, so the map does not move unsolicited.
- Browser tab visibility stops geometry ticks while hidden; foreground return jumps to the actual current time and pagehide clears the interval. These changes do not affect scheduled RF tasks or override the app's USB release behavior.
- Removed duplicate Focus selected and Show all event listeners. Added orbit_clock.mjs and tests/test_satellite_live_clock.mjs plus portable CI checks; verified JS parsing, clock mode transitions, 1-second tick, 15-second track cache and persistent Leaflet overlay updates in source. Real-time browser rendering still needs on-device visual acceptance.
- Published cache-busted v14 HTML/CSS/JS and orbit clock to gh-pages without merging the draft source into main.
### v0.15 — Real satellite imagery, online NASA photos, UTC file names and desktop LIVE parity
- New **7 · Satellite Images** browser/Pages panel distinguishes **received RF images** from **official online NASA imagery**. NASA DSCOVR EPIC and historical ISS images fetched only on click from official APIs, with provider acquisition dates, original links, optional attributed downloads, and EUMETSAT/NOAA/NASA Worldview links. Never labels public web photos as received through SDR.
- New experimental Robot36 (320×240) decoder accepts real FM-demodulated SSTV WAV with 1200Hz sync train, or user-selected/last genuine CU8 processed through bounded browser narrowband-FM demodulation. PNG gallery/save requires aligned scanlines; satellite identity, VIS verification and image fidelity are NOT guaranteed. Relevant ARISS events used 437.550 MHz Robot36; 145.800 MHz is not an always-on SSTV image service.
- Meteor-M2-3/M2-4 received LRPT remains supported by optional installed SatDump: 72k/80k modes, actual returned PNG/JPG gallery/download, no synthetic images. CU8 legacy filename compatibility preserved; external decoder still required for Meteor on Pages-only browser.
- All browser raw IQ and installed Python native captures now use satellite **CANDIDATE** or **UNATTRIBUTED**, UTC YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ, frequency Hz, optional sample rate, and media/decoder type in filenames. Derived Robot36 PNG downloads preserve original recording's UTC/satellite/frequency where embedded metadata is available.
- Native local companion on Linux/Pop!_OS/Debian, Raspberry Pi OS, macOS Apple Silicon and Windows serves the exact same browser source modules under safe path-confined same-origin /browser/ with opt-in **Open live map and Satellite Images** iframe, same 1-second LIVE and paused Sky/Earth tracking. Avoids duplicate divergent desktop live map logic; receiver ownership remains exclusive.
- Added source-attributed metadata handling, audio demodulator and Robot36 modules, browser gallery UI, Python capture naming, Python local static asset route and cross-platform synthetic tests. 240-line synthetic Robot36 audio constructed a 320×240 candidate in code; HTML UI controls and JS parsing verified. The radio path and official API CORS/limits remain untested on real hardware.
- Published updated browser app, imagery modules and desktop hosted entry to gh-pages (latest commit f6d05f922cf6abf71c75a70074e7fd5d6eaf957d). Python native companion changes are in the source feature branch, NOT the static Pages branch and NOT merged into main. Cross-platform CI remains subject to GitHub runner scheduling.

pr_records.title: Implement opt-in FM RDS and DAB Band III automatic station discovery
pr_records.body:
## Purpose
Turn the old energy-only spectrum survey into a **separate advanced tool** while adding real FM and DAB+ receiver-backed auto-discovery in **Radio Data (400)**. Responds to the user's actual Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5 FM/DAB reception: visible RF peaks are not a station list; welle-cli successfully decoded WDR NRW 11D FIC and audio services.

## Implemented
- **FM Auto Scan:** user-controlled full 87.5–108 MHz `rtl_power` survey, more sensitive candidate extraction (4 dB / 1.8 MAD), bounded quick/extended RDS tune candidates on 100-kHz grid, *real* sequential `rtl_fm | redsea` 10s verification. Only decoded station PS labels become results; original RadioText remains source-attributed and archived. Up to 16 or 48 tune trials, not a guarantee of exhaustive FM station discovery.
- **DAB+ Auto Scan:** full standard Band III channel roster 5A–13F, or only channels indicated by the user's last DAB spectrum survey. Explicitly consented, bounded local `welle-cli` POST /channel retuning, GET /mux.json welle endpoint identity validation, actual decoded FIC ensemble/services/DLS, optional return to starting channel if no external retune. Does not start/stop welle-cli or touch an unrelated SDR process. DLS archived only with decoder timestamps.
- **Interactive UI:** two scan cards with mode, consent, live progress, stop, actual confirmed stations, and post-scan per-block **TUNE THIS BLOCK FOR LISTENING** plus link to the original welle-cli service player. Original manual spectrum survey, FM RDS, FM audio and DAB read-only bridge remain.
- **Safety:** closed localhost endpoints, same-origin CSRF on POST, no new WAN listener, no default background scanning, no Internet station names, no TX, no uncontrolled third-party process kill; browser heartbeat cancels unobserved scans.
- **Unit tests:** mocked FM power/RDS and welle-cli FIC flow, original channel restoration, tuner consent, HTTP safety and bounded tuning.

## Honest limitations
- Full FM band is **surveyed**, but *only up to 16/48 promising frequencies are RDS-verified*; non-RDS/weak channels may be absent.
- welle-cli **must already be launched by user** on port 7979 and be exclusively controlled by that user. The full DAB scan **will interrupt existing welle listening**, but restoration is attempted. No automatic USB lease preemption.
- MOT slides are not produced by power scans: the existing read-only DAB bridge can fetch available slides from the currently tuned service; image reception depends on broadcaster/carousel dwell. Built-in DAB continuous audio proxy is not added; link opens the working welle-cli player.
- No physical SDR/RF reception claim from GitHub CI. Real Pop!_OS / NESDR / welle-cli hardware acceptance and browser accessibility review are required before merge.

## Validation
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, `python3 -m compileall -q textcenter tests`, `node --check web/app.js`; plus real user-initiated FM and DAB scan/cancel/restore acceptance. Preserve existing files and unrelated Survival Kit/Flight Radar services. Keep draft until all gates pass.

Relevant source: [welle-cli manual](https://manpages.debian.org/unstable/welle.io/welle-cli.1.en.html), [welle CLI upstream source](https://github.com/AlbrechtL/welle.io/blob/master/src/welle-cli/webradiointerface.cpp).

## Integration and verification update — 2026-11-06
- Kept all recently added live FM, DVB/TV, subtitles, offline translation, AI compute, and postprocessing work from main snapshot `89608300021fe8bd5f880f49c5df0e58a8043a79`; no main-branch modifications.
- Auto scanner branch merge HEAD: `c85b34293fa3f5bd67d435938c8b2d3602a88c73` (merge of scanned feature and main-backed integration tree).
- GitHub Actions completed successfully on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 for the merged HEAD: https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42156457464 and https://github.com/Tihulu/TIHULU-TEXT-CENTER/actions/runs/42156452689
- New verified FM/DAB station directory persists in SQLite; raw power peaks never become official or verified stations.
- Remain **DRAFT / UNMERGED** until owner performs explicit physical reception, stop/restore, and on-device browser checks. FM RDS detection is candidate-limited; DAB auto-scanning retunes an existing user-owned welle-cli receiver, then returns to the original channel when safe. MOT images and embedded DAB playback remain dependent on separate decoder/player bridge.

pr_records.title: Fix FM WAV player blocked by CSP and add explicit download
pr_records.body:
## User-visible failure
The FM panel reports `Capture: COMPLETED · 11.1 sec recorded` but Firefox shows `0:00 / 0:00` and no playable audio. The WAV pipeline records bytes, but the loopback server sends `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` without `media-src`. Browsers fall back to `default-src` and block the same-origin HTML audio element. See MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/media-src

## Fix (additive, no lost features)
- Explicitly allow **same-origin only** WAV playback using `media-src 'self'`. Keep `default-src 'none'` and all other CSP protections unchanged.
- Load the audio metadata so Firefox can show WAV duration; display a readable error on media load failure.
- Add **DOWNLOAD WAV** only when `clip_ready` for a completed FM capture. This saves to the browser's Downloads via an explicit user click; preserve existing in-memory capture policy and never pretend the server auto-archives audio.
- Validate the optional audio session query so an old clip URL cannot accidentally play a newer receiver capture.
- Add mock, source-free HTTP regression coverage: CSP header, valid WAV bytes/sample rate, session matching/mismatch. Existing security/receiver ownership unaffected.

## Test plan
Run existing Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 unittest matrix and JS syntax checks in GitHub Actions. Physically re-check Firefox/Pop!_OS on the user's RTL-SDR: capture FM at 98.6 MHz **only if** welle-cli, readsb and protected recordings have released the receiver; expect duration >0 and playable WAV. Check DOWNLOAD WAV yields the actual clip on disk. CI synthetic PCM is not proof of real RF audio quality.

## Usage
Restart the Python web server (old CSP headers persist until restart) and hard-reload the browser. Do not start FM capture while welle-cli owns the single SDR. Keep this draft unmerged until tests and UI validation.

## TIHULU TEXT CENTER v0.5 — Continuous AV & local translation (draft)

This is an additive implementation on the existing standalone repository. No Survival Kit/Flight Radar repository or main branch is modified.

### Implementation
- **Live FM**: one physical RTL-SDR, indefinite until stop/disconnect (24-hour safety timeout), MP3 streaming through rtl_fm + ffmpeg. Optional original MP3 archiving; no default recording.
- **Live DVB TV**: actual Hauppauge USB + frontend identification, operator-scanned DVB channels file, dvbv5-zap service-specific audio/video PIDs, FFmpeg H.264/AAC fragmented-MP4, browser MediaSource, optional original transport-stream recording.
- **Live bilingual captioning**: same receiver PCM (no second SDR reader), local multilingual faster-whisper ASR, English/German/Turkish and all six translation directions via offline installed Argos packages. Source and translated layers, save-original/save-translation independent consent, later translate original, SRT/VTT export.
- **Compute**: show named CPU, GPU and Hailo NPU devices, separate automatic/manual ASR and translation device selection. CUDA requires verified CTranslate2 runtime. NPU is detected but deliberately disabled until a validated vendor speech/translation adapter exists.
- **Resource controls**: audio and video tuning are user-approved, cooperative lock and candidate competitor detection. No default background scanning/recording/ASR, no remote model APIs/download, finite queues and disk quotas.
- **UI**: responsive Live Studio P420, device inventory, play/stop, source and target languages, recorded media, caption archive.
- **Documentation**: docs/LIVE_STUDIO.md, README and Survival Kit master handoff updated.

### Mandatory acceptance before merging into main
- [ ] Full GitHub Actions CI matrix green (Python 3.11/3.12/3.13, JS syntax)
- [ ] Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5: real continuous mono FM browser playback and MP3 recording; must not interrupt readsb/Flight Radar.
- [ ] Hauppauge 01589 (on arrival): USB, firmware, correct DVB frontend, regional scan, service-specific TS, fMP4 browser playback and lossless TS recording.
- [ ] CPU/CUDA: local multilingual model and Argos language packs physically installed and verified; translations EN↔DE, EN↔TR, DE↔TR; model unavailable must fail clearly.
- [ ] RTL-SDR and DVB shared lease integration with real Survival Kit broker; current /proc+flock are conservative interim checks, not a universal lease authority.
- [ ] iOS/Android and desktop media compatibility, buffering, CPU/RAM/power and storage limits validated.
- [ ] Hailo AI HAT+2 ASR/translation runtime only after a compatible tested backend exists; never claim available just because detected.

**Not claimed:** physical RF/DVB acceptance, universal browser support, zero-latency subtitles, generic NPU acceleration or authenticated mobile network service. Do not merge to Survival Kit production until these gates pass.

pr_records.title: Fix DAB MOT image save feedback, live gallery refresh and channel attribution
pr_records.body:
## User report
DAB frequencies are visible but received images do not appear or save. The current read-only DAB receiver bridge only has channel attribution for 5C/11D, silently catches image fetch failures, and only renders the gallery at page load. Also, an RF power peak is not evidence of an actual DAB ensemble or a transmitted MOT image.

## Changes
- Expand the **standard DAB Band III frequency-centre lookup** to include 5C, 8B, 9D, 11D and all other nominal standard Band III blocks. This does **not** assume any station is on-air; the decoder still needs a real service and original image timestamp.
- Return per-service MOT image states (`saved`, `not_broadcast`, `empty`, `failed`, `not_requested`, `frequency_unknown`) and bounded aggregate counters. Continue rejecting corrupt and oversized images.
- When a real image is saved via explicit **READ RUNNING DAB RECEIVER**, show its preview in the corresponding service result and refresh the offline image gallery immediately (without duplicate panels or restarting the page).
- Show save vs no-transmission vs fetch/format errors distinctly; never fetch internet artwork or invent signal/station names.
- Add decoder/mock tests and exact operator instructions. Keep welle-cli launch, retuning and decoder installation **outside** this read-only adapter and preserve all other RF functionality.

## Remaining physical requirement
The user screenshot explicitly reports `welle-cli: not installed / not on PATH`. This PR does not and **cannot** save an actual DAB MOT slide unless welle-cli is independently installed, running on loopback, synchronized to a real station transmitting valid MOT image data, and the RTL-SDR is free from protected Flight Radar/readsb and recording sessions. A DAB energy survey is not a decoder. See existing `docs/RADIO_AND_DVB.md`.

## Tests / non-claims
CI: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, JS syntax and Python compile checks. Synthetic test images do not establish real hardware reception; genuine on-air validation is still pending. Preserve PR #4 clickable spectral-block workflow separately; this PR is based on current `main` including its read-only DAB bridge, not the older PR #4 branch. Do not merge until reviewed and green.
